messages:
tara: Postmortem action sync: we need clearer ownership on canary blast-radius limits and auto-rollback. Recent incident shows we lacked a global fallback and the flag metadata was inconsistent. Proposing owners + small deliverables.
ben: I can handle standardizing flag metadata + validation during deploys. Will add a schema and a lint check in CI. ETA: 5 days.
ishaan: I'll take automation for auto-rollback. Plan: two-signal requirement (errors + latency) and a minimum sustained window. Also add a safelist so certain critical customers aren't affected. ETA: 2 weeks.
ops-bot: incident-bot: pm 812 resolved. Postmortem created: https://redwood/postmortems/812. Please add follow-ups.
tara: Good. Also need a lightweight global kill switch for emergencies. Ops will own runbook and the UI; devtools should expose an API to flip flags quickly.
ben: Quick schema draft:
```
metadata:
  max_stage_pct: 5
  safety_window_seconds: 1800
  exempt_customers: ["acct:1234"]
  auto_rollback:
    enable: true
    error_rate_threshold: 0.03
    latency_threshold_ms: 1200
    sustained_seconds: 180
```
ishaan: We'll make the auto-rollback callable by the runtime or by external monitor. Also: backoff strategy when rollback fails to fully stop traffic.
tara: Action item list: flag schema + CI lint (ben) 5d; auto-rollback implementation + tests (ishaan) 14d; panic button + runbook (ops) 7d. Add a quarterly incident-pattern review.
ops-bot: reminder: link PRs to postmortem 812.
ben: Will add a pre-deploy check that warns if a flag lacks the metadata. Also add a default policy if missing.
ishaan: I'll implement metrics emission for "active_rollout_percent" so the incident team can see real-time impact.
tara: OK, thanks. Please update the postmortem with links before EOD Friday. We'll review next Monday in the ops sync.
